Encoding and normalisation notes.

Text that survives a transformation is still the same text. Percent-encoding,
base64, hexadecimal and JSON string escapes are reversible; case folding and
Unicode normalisation are lossy in one direction but preserve identity for most
practical comparison.

A scanner that compares only literal bytes will miss every one of these forms. A
scanner that decodes them will find the same content in each. Neither behaviour
is a statement about meaning: a paraphrase of a sentence is not a transformation
of it, and no decoder recovers one from the other.

Composition matters. Base64 of a percent-encoded decomposed form requires three
reversals to recover, and a decoder that applies only one will report a clean
result on material it did not actually inspect.
